By joining our Talent Pool, you can let us know you're interested in future opportunities at Sparta and you're giving us permission to reach out to you when a role opens up that we feel could match your experience or interests.

When you apply we will review your application against anything we're hiring for right now. We'll keep your details in our system and if we feel there's a potential match now or in the near future we'll reach out to you.

If at any time you change your mind and want us to delete your data, please get in touch and let us know!

Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not.

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

Fall in love with the problem

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to.

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

It's your fault. Lucky you.

If it's on you, it's in your control.

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

Conflict is a gift

Honesty is an expression of care.

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

data.title: Junior Transformation Strategist (UK Based)
data.description:
About Duvo

Before Duvo, our founders built and ran a $2 billion retailer. They saw how much critical work still depended on spreadsheets, inboxes, supplier portals and the memory of experienced operators. The real process rarely lived in one system. People held the last mile together.

Duvo is building the Enterprise Execution OS: the shared layer that understands how work really runs, carries it across existing systems and measures the business result.

Our agents do the work, not just suggest the next step. They gather evidence, make decisions within agreed rules, route exceptions to the right person and update the source system. People keep control wherever judgment or approval is needed. Every action leaves an audit trail.

We start with one recurring process and a clear outcome. Every solution carries a contracted 5x ROI guarantee.

The role

As a Junior Transformation Strategist, you are the insight and output engine beside our Transformation Strategists on our largest accounts.

On bigger engagements we need more than technical delivery. We need someone who can take a messy process, find the critical question, get to a clear insight fast, and put it into materials a customer team will act on. Today that work often lands on Forward Deployed Engineers. That is the wrong use of a scarce technical resource. This role exists so that insight work has a dedicated owner.

You will work alongside Transformation Strategists (who own day-to-day account presence and workstream direction) and Forward Deployed Engineers (who own the technical solution). You do not own the executive relationship or the commercial outcome. You own the speed and quality of the analytical and written work that makes those conversations possible.

This is a fungible problem-solving role. You will be thrown at different accounts and different problem types (category, supply chain, finance ops, inventory, commercial) and expected to produce. Ideal for someone currently ~2–4 years into a client-facing career as an Associate, Senior Associate, or Consultant at McKinsey or BCG who wants concentrated ownership, not another staffing cycle.

We want to hire two people into this role quickly.

What you will do

1. Get to the insight

  • Dive into how work actually happens: interviews, extracts, handoffs, exceptions and the workarounds people use to keep things running.

  • Build a fact base that shows where cost, cash, service, cycle time or control is being lost.

  • Form a hypothesis early, name what would kill it, and pressure-test it with the Transformation Strategist before you polish anything.

  • Structure unfamiliar problems without waiting for a perfect brief. Frame the selection equation (what matters, what does not) so the team and the customer can decide.

2. Deliver output that moves a decision

  • Turn analysis into decision-ready slides, one-pagers and memos that make the important choice obvious.

  • Be exact about baselines, assumptions and evidence. Do not use polish to hide uncertainty.

  • Work fast: same-day or next-day turnarounds on defined asks are the norm, not the exception.

  • Produce materials a Transformation Strategist can take into a working session or steerco with minimal rewrite.

3. Be fungible surge capacity on big accounts

  • Plug into multiple live enterprise accounts as extra hands where the Transformation Strategist needs analytical depth.

  • Jump between problem types without needing a long ramp each time.

  • Keep a clean trail of actions, open questions and evidence so work can be handed between you, the Transformation Strategist and the FDE without loss.

  • Surface blockers early; do not sit on ambiguity hoping it resolves.

4. Build the evidence for impact

  • Help lock baseline, target and measurement window before implementation.

  • Quantify results in language a CFO would trust (revenue, margin, cost, working capital, cycle time, control), not activity counts or sentiment.

  • Investigate misses as carefully as wins, and turn both into clear evidence packs the Transformation Strategist can use upstairs.

5. Stay close to the customer team (working level)

  • Own relationships with operators and mid-level owners who live the process day to day.

  • Prepare working sessions, capture decisions and follow commitments through.

  • Know when a question needs a senior call and escalate early rather than bluffing.

You will not own commercial negotiations, board-level relationships or technical build. You will own the craft and pace of the insight work that makes those outcomes possible.

Skills and capabilities we will assess

These are explicit. We will hire against them.

  • Structured problem solving. Hypothesis-driven. You can take an unfamiliar operation apart, find the critical question, write a kill criterion, and give a clear recommendation without hiding behind a framework.

  • Analytical speed and numeracy. Comfortable with messy data and incomplete information. You build analyses that are concise, correct and decision-ready under time pressure.

  • Written and slide craft. Your decks and memos are tight. First page says the answer. Evidence follows. A partner or Transformation Strategist can use your output with light edit, not a rewrite.

  • Insight generation. You do not stop at describing the process. You find where value is lost and what to change first.

  • Fungibility. You can be dropped onto a new account or a new problem type and produce within days, not weeks.

  • Delivery bias. You stay after the framing is done. You follow actions through. You notice what is not working and help fix it.

  • Customer judgment at working level. You listen well, ask a direct question and communicate clearly with operators and managers. You know when to escalate.

  • AI-native personal workflow. You use AI seriously to accelerate research, analysis and drafting, and you remain responsible for the quality of what goes in front of a customer.

  • Early-stage working style. You move without perfect instructions, write in plain English and surface bad news early.

Who we are looking for

  • Currently an Associate, Senior Associate or Consultant (or equivalent) at McKinsey or BCG, typically ~2–4 years of core, client-facing consulting experience. Bain and other top strategy firms can fit if the craft is the same.

  • A track record of producing high-quality analyses and slides that partners and clients actually used to decide.

  • Evidence you can work quickly without sacrificing rigor.

  • Comfort operating as surge capacity across problems rather than owning a single long study end to end alone.

Helpful but not required: retail, CPG, supply chain, logistics, inventory or finance operations exposure; prior startup or early-stage experience.

What good looks like after 12 months

  • Transformation Strategists on our largest accounts treat you as the person they call when they need a sharp fact base, a clean deck or a second pair of eyes on an insight, within hours not days.

  • You have supported multiple accounts and problem types without losing quality.

  • At least one measured process change carries analysis and evidence you built.

  • Your templates, diagnostics and slide patterns are reused by the next Junior Transformation Strategist.

  • FDEs on those accounts spend their time on technical delivery, not insight decks.

This role is not for you if

  • You want to own the C-level relationship, commercial negotiation or full transformation roadmap from day one. That is the Transformation Strategist / Senior path.

  • You only enjoy the framing phase and lose interest once the work becomes detailed.

  • You need perfectly clean data, a large analyst team or complete instructions before you can make progress.

  • You see slides as the final product rather than a tool to help a customer decide and act.

  • You want to build automations or live in the technical weeds. That is the Forward Deployed Engineer role.

  • You want a narrow, single-account BA role with little variety or visible accountability.

Why leave McKinsey or BCG for this

  • Your insight work lands in live enterprise operations with a contracted 5x ROI, not in a forgotten sharepoint.

  • You sit beside Transformation Strategists and FDEs on real accounts, so you see recommendation through to adoption.

  • You get concentrated ownership of analytical craft instead of being staffed for utilization.

  • Direct access to founders, customers and decisions in a small team.

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, with flexibility between cash and ownership.

  • A clear path: strong Juniors become Transformation Strategists who own day-to-day account momentum.

How we work

  • Own it. The bar is not “I flagged it.” It is “I moved it forward.” An 80% fix today often beats a perfect answer next week.

  • Stay close to the customer. Know their real day better than the process document.

  • Prove it and say it straight. Measure before you propose. Share bad news when you have it.

  • Use AI and work in public. We use AI on our own work and remain responsible for the output. We write things down in English so someone who missed the meeting can still follow.

  • Bring intensity and judgment. A good answer can still lose if it arrives too late. The pace is high because the team is small and the customer work is live.

Location and travel

This role is UK-based. You will need to be living in the UK, or relocating there before you start, and able to travel to client sites from there. Expect regular travel and periods on site with customers for several days in a week when projects are live.

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, with flexibility in the balance between cash and ownership.

  • Direct access to founders, customers and decisions.

  • The budget and autonomy to use the best AI tools available.

  • A product already producing measured results in live enterprise operations.

  • The chance to build a career at the intersection of consulting, operations and AI-led transformation.

How we hire

We respect your time and move fast:

  1. Screening call.

  2. Hiring manager interview. Fit on problem-solving craft, pace and whether this is the right altitude for you.

  3. Case study panel. A live enterprise problem that tests structure, numbers, prioritisation and clear communication (including slide / written output).

  4. CEO interview. A candid discussion about the role, Duvo and whether this is the environment for you.

We move quickly and give direct feedback throughout.

data.title: Mechatronics Engineer
data.description:
About CircuitHub

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

The role

Mechatronics Engineers at CircuitHub own projects end to end. You'll start with a problem, often on our factory floor, and take it all the way to a working machine:

  • Understand the problem and turn it into a clear specification

  • Generate ideas and choose the right mechanism

  • Design it in CAD and prove it out with the engineering calculations

  • Prototype and build it, machining parts in our in-house CNC shop

  • Bring it to life with software on our in-house robotics operating system

We work AI-first. AI tools help you scope the problem, drive your CAD, run the calculations and write the machine software. The software side needs basic software engineering skills, not a software background: you'll write it with AI agents, supported by a dedicated software engineering team who build the operating system.

You must have built things before, ideally robots, whether as a hobbyist, student, employee or founder. We don't hire narrow specialists. We want engineers who can:

  • Diagnose system-wide failures from first principles

  • Prototype mechanical and software fixes on the fly

  • Work autonomously and communicate clearly with a team spread across sites

  • Take responsibility for how their machines perform in live production

Things you'll do

This is a design role with hands-on prototyping. For example:

  • Conceive new mechanisms to handle electronics parts and other robotic handling tasks, using AI to scope and specify the problem

  • Design gantries and end effectors in Fusion 360

  • Use AI agents to run the engineering calculations, and know when to distrust them

  • Machine prototype parts in our in-house CNC shop

  • Analyse end-effector behaviour from video and revise its geometry and control approach to improve throughput and reliability

  • Program machine behaviour on our in-house robotics operating system, with AI agents doing the heavy lifting

  • Specify sensors that catch errors while a machine is running, or monitor a chemical process

  • Prototype and deploy a new test robot for in-line PCB validation

  • Commission your machines and hand them over to our build team to scale up

  • Work across our US and UK sites to share what you've learned and shape the roadmap

Bonus skills

  • Experience programming machines, whether PLCs, robot controllers, embedded systems or Python

  • Programming and running CNC machinery

  • Design of chemical handling machinery

  • Optics

Pay and level

£45K–£125K depending on experience, plus equity.

A candidate at the lower end of the range might have:

  • Built some systems before, with some exposure to robotics or automation

  • Seen parts and subsystems through to manufacture as part of a design team

  • Knowledge of designing for machining

  • A keen interest in moving their career towards practical robotics

A candidate at the upper end might also have:

  • Led the build and deployment of large-scale automated systems

  • Written the software that controls their own machines

  • Designed for a wide range of manufacturing methods, from machining to sheet metal to injection moulding

  • Mentored more junior engineers

The range isn't a hard limit: if you're an expert in all of the above, we still want to talk to you. Not quite so experienced but passionate and keen to learn? Talk to us too.

Location

Full-time on-site at one of our UK sites:

  • Cambridge: our central Cambridge site, alongside the team designing, building and expanding the Grid.

  • London: our London site.

Compensation: £45K – £125K • Offers Equity

  • Cambridge and London • £45K – £125K • Offers Equity

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

What We’re Looking For

We are assembling a team of system build engineers to scale the production of our factory automation systems. We are looking for people who are excited to build robotics, whether that be high speed gantries, novel end effectors, custom assembly tooling, laser enclosures, chemical handling systems and everything in between. If you love to build things, this role could be for you!

 

Critically, you should be comfortable interpreting 3D CAD assemblies and building from them directly. We use Fusion 360, but a basic familiarity with Fusion 360 or other leading CAD systems (Solidworks, Inventor, Creo, Catia, NX, Onshape) in a professional or hobbyist setting is a must.

 

Experience with PLC commissioning/debugging, particularly Beckhoff TwinCAT, CNC machining and cabinet wiring would be bonuses here.

 

This role would be excellent for (but not limited to!) recent graduates, newly qualified apprentices, maintenance technicians, machinists, makers and more. If you want to build things and can spin CAD we want to hear from you.

 

We are flexible on how you want to work; this is a hands-on, onsite role but the hours and schedule aren’t rigid. We would be delighted to accommodate part time or adjusted schedules to suit caring/childcare or other obligations outside of work. Would you prefer a non-traditional work schedule? Talk to us!

 

What you’ll do

  • Build up full automation systems from a mixture of custom and off-the-shelf parts, anything from hand-held end effectors to multi-tonne high speed gantries

  • Take a role in commissioning and testing

  • Liaise with logistics partners for system shipment

  • Work through any design issues by feeding back to the design team and making your own design changes

  • General workshop tasks such as tidying, consumable stocking and machinery cleaning

 

What CircuitHub Can Offer

Salary, £35,000 - £60,000 dependent on experience

 

A candidate at the lower end of this range might be expected to:

  • Be able to build mechatronic assemblies from 3D CAD

  • Carry out basic troubleshooting tasks such as selecting the correct fasteners, torquing to the correct values, pressing bearings and feeding back design issues to the wider team.

  • Work safely in a dynamic, constantly evolving workshop environment

 

A candidate at the higher end of this range might additionally be able to do some of the following:

  • carry out small component design changes as part of assembly troubleshooting

  • Carry out some TwinCAT drive commissioning

  • Be confident in basic troubleshooting of a wiring cabinet

  • Set up/program a CNC mill

 

Think you can do more than this? Great! The salary range is not a hard limit, if you are an expert on all of the above we still want to talk to you.

 

Not quite so experienced, but passionate and want to learn? Also great! Talk to us, we might be able to find a place for you.

 

Location

This is an onsite role out of our site in central Cambridge working alongside a driven team of automation engineers who are designing, building and supporting the expansion of our Grid PCB assembly system.

Compensation: £35K – £60K • Offers Equity

data.title: People Experience Program Manager
data.description:
About Fundamental

Fundamental is an AI research lab pioneering the future of enterprise decision-making. Our flagship model, NEXUS is the world's most powerful Large Tabular Model (LTM) - purpose-built for the structured records that contain trillions of dollars in business value. With $275m in funding from leading investors and trusted by Fortune 100 companies, Fundamental is giving businesses the Power to Predict.

At Fundamental, you'll work on unprecedented technical challenges in foundation model development and build technology that transforms how the world's largest companies make decisions. This is your opportunity to be part of a category-defining company from the ground-up. Join the team defining the future of enterprise AI.

About the role

Our People & Talent team is building from scratch to support a category shaping company that has rapidly grown and continues to hire at pace. Reporting directly to the Global Head of Talent, you will manage the full employee journey including pre-onboarding, onboarding, benefits, people development and day-to-day people operations.

At Fundamental we see people and talent operations as a core product, and you'll shape how everyone experiences it. We are energised to work alongside exceptionally talented people, so the care and support we offer should match that standard. This means creating seamless offers, smooth first-week onboardings, clear and meaningful career pathways, and proactive answers before anyone has to ask. You will have the space to rethink existing processes rather than just maintain them, and actively automate repetitive tasks. By removing manual work where possible, you will free up time to focus on the human touches that truly matter.

What makes this role so dynamic is our global context. Everything you design needs to feel personal, thoughtful, and clear, to the candidates and employees you support. While working asynchronously is necessary for us, staying connected and unified is something this role will intentionally foster.

What you'll do

  • Guide new team members through a seamless onboarding journey (from contract signing through their first months), ensuring everyone feels equally welcomed and supported

  • Carefully support key career and life milestones, including promotions, parental leave, relocations, and transitions, by coordinating smoothly behind the scenes with local partners

  • Maintain our People Ops stack so team members can rely on accurate, clear information about their roles and details, keeping key integrations aligned to remove friction across systems

  • Enhance and champion our benefits offerings, making sure every option is easy to understand, access, and appreciate across all regions

  • Serve as a trusted point of contact for employee questions, offering warm, prompt support while turning common inquiries into clearer documentation and simpler processes

  • Streamline repetitive tasks with thoughtful automation and AI tools, freeing up more time to focus on meaningful, personal human touchpoints

  • Foster an inclusive asynchronous workplace through intuitive self-serve guides and clear written communication that respects diverse time zones

  • Listen to employee feedback throughout the onboarding and lifecycle journey, using insights to continually refine and elevate the team experience

  • Collaborate with the Talent team to create a welcoming, cohesive transition from candidate experience to day-one onboarding

  • Nurture our distributed culture through performance development, engagement initiatives, and shared moments that bring people together

  • Ensure a safe, fair, and compliant environment across regions, handling sensitive matters with care and sound judgment

About you

  • Organised. You keep track of complex projects across multiple time zones without dropping the ball, and you prefer building reliable systems over relying on memory.

  • Thoughtful. You naturally put yourself in other people's shoes. Whether it is understanding a new hire's night-before nerves, giving a manager what they need to deliver feedback, or writing guidelines that are clear and accessible, you pay attention to the details that make people feel supported.

  • Tech fluent. You are comfortable working with People tech, tools and data. You can look at onboarding feedback or team data, pull out meaningful insights, and back up your suggestions with consistent numbers. You naturally seek out smarter ways to work and actively use AI tools to streamline your day-to-day workflow.

  • Clear communicator. Much of what you create will be read by teammates in different time zones, often working in a second language. You write plainly, warmly, and concisely, taking time to edit your work before sharing it.

  • Low ego. You step in wherever help is needed to get things done. You appreciate direct communication, adapt quickly when new facts emerge, and thrive in an environment with plenty of room to build.

What we're looking for

  • 4+ years in People Operations, Talent, Recruiting, or Program Management, ideally in a fast-paced tech environment

  • Hands-on experience configuring and managing people workflows, data, and reporting

  • Experience supporting international team members or candidates, developing processes that optimise for ideal experiences

  • A clear track record of simplifying or rebuilding inefficient operational processes

  • Comfortable pulling and analysing team data to inform everyday decision-making

  • Strong written communication skills across docs, Slack, and written guides

  • High discretion and sound judgment when handling confidential information

  • Ability to work independently and thrive in a distributed team environment

Where you could stand out

  • You have seen a company grow quickly, so you know firsthand how that feels for the colleagues you work with

  • You enjoy setting up smart automations using AI, no-code, or scripting tools, and can walk us through something you built

  • You bring personal experience from a remote-first team, along with clear ideas on what helps new joiners succeed asynchronously

  • You have touched benefits design or renewals across more than one region

  • You have partnered closely with recruiting or interacted with tools like Ashby

  • You have helped run broader people initiatives beyond core operations, like performance reviews, engagement surveys, or manager development

data.title: Faculty Fellowship - Data Science - UK - January 2027
data.description:
Why Faculty?


We established Faculty in 2014 because we thought that AI would be the most important technology of our time. Since then, we’ve worked with over 350 global customers to transform their performance through human-centric AI. You can read about our real-world impact here.

 

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

 

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

 

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

Why the Faculty Fellowship?

 

Artificial Intelligence is the defining technology of our age, but it is only valuable when applied to the real world. Since 2014, Faculty has helped over 500 PhDs, postdocs and engineers transition into high-impact careers in data science and machine learning.

 

How it works:

  • 2 Weeks of Intensive Training: Learn to apply your advanced technical knowledge to real-world data science problems.

  • 6 Week Paid Placement: Tackle a commercial data science project with a host company (paid at the London Living Wage).

  • Demo Day Finale: Present your work to 100+ guests and industry leaders from across the UK and Europe.

     

Where our alumni go: Our alumni have gone on to shape the future at companies like Google, Meta, Tesco, and AstraZeneca, as well as disruptive startups like PhysicsX and Orbital Witness. We are also incredibly proud that a high percentage of fellows choose to continue their journey internally, joining the Faculty team permanently.

 

About the role

 

As a Fellow at Faculty, you will join an elite cohort transforming industries through cutting-edge data science. This intensive, eight-week programme bridges academia and real-world impact, embedding you directly into high-stakes commercial environments.

You will apply advanced machine learning techniques to solve complex, ambiguous problems for our clients, turning theoretical knowledge into high-value deployable solutions. It is a fast-paced launchpad designed to accelerate your technical growth, build exceptional commercial acumen, and empower you to shape the future of artificial intelligence in an ambitious, forward-thinking tech community.

 

Who we're looking for:

  • You hold a finished PhD or Master’s degree in a STEM subject, complemented by a strong foundation in data science or machine learning.

  • You possess a high level of mathematical competence alongside solid experience with theoretical concepts like hypothesis testing, Bayesian inference, and neural networks.

  • You demonstrate strong programming skills, particularly in Python, and feel comfortable navigating core data science coding libraries.

  • You bring an entrepreneurial mindset, showing the resilience and autonomy needed to structure your own project plans and hit critical deadlines.

  • You can communicate complex technical ideas clearly, adapting your language seamlessly for both technical peers and non-technical partners.

  • You thrive in fast-paced, ambitious environments, showing curiosity and a relentless drive to learn and deploy new technologies.

 

Requirements

  • Right to Work: We are unfortunately unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role, so you will need to hold full-time UK right to work to apply. If your eligibility is based on a visa, just pop the details of your situation into your application so we can review it. To learn more about your options, check out www.gov.uk.

  • Location & Logistics: This is a fully in-person, eight-week programme based in London, so you will need to be able to commute daily for the entire duration. Please keep in mind that Faculty is unable to provide or reimburse accommodation and travel expenses.

 

Our Timelines

  • 17th November 2026 (17:00 BST): Application Deadline.

  • Mid November: Coding tests sent via email.

  • End of November: Interviews held remotely online.

  • 18th December: Final notifications sent to all applicants.

  • Monday 25th January - Friday 19th March : Programme duration (Full-time, Monday–Friday).

*Please note that the program dates are tentative and may be adjusted or postponed entirely. We will notify all applicants immediately should any changes occur to the dates or the program schedule. We appreciate your flexibility and understanding.

 

What the Fellowship offers

 

  • Fully Paid: Earn the London Living Wage for the full eight weeks.

  • Expert-Led Training: Two weeks of immersive lectures followed by weekly Friday masterclasses, bridging the gap between academic theory and commercial data science.

  • Dedicated Mentorship: Receive ongoing support and guidance from experienced Faculty practitioners, gaining insight into how AI and data science are applied to solve real-world business challenges while developing your technical, commercial and communication skills.

  • Real-World Value: A dedicated six-week placement embedded with a business, tackling a high-stakes data science challenge.

  • Career Launchpad: A proven pathway into industry, backed by more than a decade of helping technically exceptional individuals successfully transition into industry across tech, startups, and the FTSE 100.

  • Unrivalled Networking: Connect with a 500+ strong alumni community and pitch your project to 100+ industry guests at Demo Day.

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

data.description:
About Kyra

Kyra is an enterprise influencer marketing platform working with brands like SharkNinja, Coach, H&M, Ray-Ban, and Converse. Our platform manages the full lifecycle — creator discovery, campaign management, content review, payments, analytics, and AI-powered intelligence across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.


📍London (Hybrid)
💰 Competitive, dependent on experience

The Opportunity

You will be work on of one of Kyra's largest and most complex global enterprise accounts: a fast-moving, multi-category consumer brand with 12+ sub-brands, 35+ active stakeholders, and campaigns running simultaneously across multiple regions.

Your job is to keep delivery tight, keep the client happy, and be a safe pair of hands on a flagship account. This is not about growing or expanding the account. The commercial relationship is locked in. The job is world-class servicing at enterprise scale.

What you'll do:

  • Work on the global account relationship across 12+ sub-brands and multiple regions. Stay organised across a volume of comms, briefs, and stakeholders that is genuinely unusual.

  • Orchestrate cross-functional teams: creative, paid media, creator partnerships, and product. You are the connective tissue. If something drifts, you see it early and fix it.

  • If something drifts (performance, scope, relationship, or timeline) you see it early and fix it. No surprises. Steady, organised ownership.


🎯 Co-own the Relationship Work on client relationships across product launches, seasonal campaigns, and always-on programmes. Multi-thread across their teams. Build trust at every level. Have direct conversations when performance needs to improve.

📈 Turn Insight into Strategy Translate campaign data into clear, executive-level recommendations using AI to move from raw numbers to narrative faster. Present performance against KPIs (engagement, EMV, sales lift, affiliate impact) and explain what it means.

🔍 Work On Delivery End-to-End Lead client onboarding for new briefs: build decks, verify SOW accuracy, coordinate internal teams, demo the platform. Manage timelines, scopes, budgets, and execution across our full product suite, including Always-On creator partnerships, Pulse campaigns, Makers (CGC), Amplify+ (paid boosting), Seeding+, and License+. With 6+ briefs running simultaneously, operational precision is everything. Keep work on-brand, on-time, and within margin.

📊 Protect & Grow Revenue Lead post-campaign analysis: run internal post-mortems, build PCA decks, present performance narratives. Work on exec-ready reporting (QBRs/EBRs). Reporting should inform decisions, not just recap them.

🛡️ Keep the System Tight Keep tracking clean. Watch capacity. Fix what's inefficient. Make sure client feedback doesn't get lost. Feed client insights back into product development.

Feed Insight Back into Product Surface client needs, pain points, and feature requests back into the product team. You are the closest person to how the client actually uses the platform.

 

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who has:

  • 8+ years in influencer or creator marketing

  • Campaign execution experience. You have actually run creator marketing activations, not just managed client relationships from a distance.

  • Enterprise account servicing at scale. Multi-stakeholder, high-volume, complex. You have managed accounts with this many moving parts before.

  • Exceptional organisation. The volume of comms, briefs, regions, and stakeholders on this account is unusually high. Getting lost is easy. You don't get lost.

  • Self-starter with an entrepreneurial mindset. You'll work on learning, build internal relationships proactively, and don't wait to be told what to do.

  • Strong hands-on campaign experience, with real fluency in TikTok.

  • AI fluency, applied. Our platform is AI-powered and you'll be expected to get up to speed fast and use it daily for client summaries, performance narratives, and campaign analysis. We're looking for people already comfortable using AI tools in their workflow, so the learning curve is the platform, not the concept.

  • Comfortable working across project management tools (Asana, Airtable, Slack) and reporting dashboards.

  • CPG or multi-category consumer brand experience is a plus.

  • Bonus if you're English and Spanish bilingual speaking.

You should be commercially sharp, operationally reliable, and able to speak confidently about the accounts you've managed.

Traits That Matter
Proactive. Organised. Adaptable. Self-starting. Comfortable with ambiguity.

You don't wait for problems to land. You see them coming and act. You don't need rigid processes or hand-holding. Tools, product, and ways of working evolve constantly here, and you thrive on that.

You're willing to say "I don't know" and go find out. You take feedback well. You build trust fast.

 

Nice to have

If you speak one of these languages - Spanish, French, German, Italian

What Success Looks Like What Success Looks Like

By Month 1: You have full context on all active sub-brands, briefs, and stakeholders. You've built a strong working relationship with the Campaign Director and the internal pod. The client knows your name and trusts you to run things.

By Month 3: Delivery is running smoothly across all regions. You work on reporting and client comms without oversight. Post-campaign analysis is sharp and drives clear recommendations. Internal teams come to you, not around you.

By Month 6: The account is in better shape than when you arrived. Stakeholder satisfaction is high. Nothing has been dropped. Leadership trusts your judgement completely

💟 Support

If you have a condition or require an adjustment to our interview process - please let us know so we can make adjustments to support you. Please note that when you submit an application or resume, your data will be processed in line with our privacy policy.

About Singular Photonics

Singular Photonics is a fast-growing fabless semiconductor start-up, developing Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) sensors that bring advanced computation directly into imaging. Based at Orchard Brae House in Edinburgh, we are a close-knit team at the forefront of the photonics revolution.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Software Engineer to take a leading role in developing the Software Development Kit (SDK) for our SPAD sensors and cameras. You will build the interfaces that let customers configure our hardware, stream sensor data and turn single-photon measurements into results, supporting applications from early prototyping through to production.   • A minimum of three years’ experience designing and maintaining production software, including ownership of code through to release.

Our Mission:

Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement.

Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far.

Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies.

Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them.

Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here.

The Role

As an AI Transformation Strategist, you'll work directly with our most strategic customers to understand their objectives and key challenges, identify high-impact AI opportunities, and translate them into measurable business value.

You'll be building AI solutions on Omnea's procurement automation platform, combining the structured data flowing through requests, approvals, contracts, and supplier records with AI. Omnea gives AI the operational context of how a business actually buys, so it can move past answering questions and start taking action inside procurement itself: routing requests, flagging risk, drafting contract terms, negotiating with suppliers. There is no AI without that context.

You'll prototype these solutions, demonstrate their value to executives, and ensure successful implementation, adoption, and value realisation, growing Omnea's footprint at those customers as you go.

This customer-facing role is ideal for people who enjoy working directly with customers and turning complex business challenges into practical AI solutions. The focus is on problem framing, solution design, and business impact rather than pure implementation. While you will prototype AI solutions, the primary goal is to deliver meaningful business value to customers.

What You'll Do

  • Identify High-Impact AI Opportunities: Work closely with enterprise customers to understand their strategic priorities and operational challenges, identifying where AI can deliver measurable business value.

  • Design AI-Powered Solutions: Translate complex business problems into scalable solution architectures, using Omnea's AI to eliminate manual work across procurement.

  • Writing a sharp brief for what you want AI to build is now core to the role, not a side skill.

data.title: Head of FinOps
data.description:
About Ryft

 

Ryft is a regulated payment facilitator and authorised payment institution building the infrastructure layer for modern commerce platforms.

We enable marketplaces, SaaS platforms and multi-party ecosystems to embed and monetise payments natively. Our technology handles onboarding, compliance, orchestration, split payments and revenue sharing, allowing our partners to focus on growth while we manage complexity.

 

We are now entering the next phase of scale, expanding into new verticals and building a category-defining embedded payments platform.

 

The role

Every payment that goes through Ryft creates a trail of money moving between card schemes, acquiring banks, our accounts and our merchants. You make sure that trail adds up, every day, and that customer funds are protected exactly as the FCA requires.

You'll own Ryft's financial operations end to end: reconciliations, settlement, safeguarding and the reporting that proves it. It's a hands-on role. You'll run the daily processes yourself, then automate them, so they scale as we launch in new markets and currencies.

What you'll do

• Reconciliations: run daily reconciliations across scheme and acquirer settlement reports, bank statements and our internal ledger. Investigate and resolve breaks quickly and accurately.

• Safeguarding: own the daily internal and external safeguarding reconciliations under CASS 15, prepare the monthly safeguarding return, keep the resolution pack current and support the annual safeguarding audit.

• Settlement and payouts: make sure merchants are paid the right amount on time, across currencies, and that split payments and escrow balances tie out.

• Fees and cost of payments: reconcile interchange, scheme and acquirer fees against what we've billed, and flag where margin is leaking.

• Disputes and chargebacks: track the financial side of chargebacks, refunds and reserves.

• Month-end: feed accurate payment data into the close and work with Finance on revenue and balance sheet reconciliations.

• Automation: work with Engineering and Product to replace spreadsheets with automated recs, alerts and dashboards.

• Controls and documentation: write and maintain the SOPs, controls and evidence that auditors and the FCA will ask for.,

• Expansion: help design the finance operations for new payment flows, entities and licences, starting with our EU licence application in Malta.

What we're looking for

• 4+ years in financial operations, payment operations, treasury or reconciliations at a payments company, EMI, acquirer or fintech.

• Hands-on experience of daily reconciliations at volume with the highest level of attention to detail. You know how to investigate and resolve the root cause of a break, not just clear it.

• Working knowledge of UK safeguarding rules (PSRs 2017, EMRs 2011, CASS 15) and what an auditor expects to see.

• You understand how card payments settle: schemes, acquirers, interchange and settlement cycles.

• You'd rather build a process once than do it manually forever.

• Comfortable taking full ownership of the end-to-end process, and liaising directly with Finance, Compliance, Engineering and our banking partners.

Nice to have

• Experience in a marketplace or platform payments business (split payments, escrow, payouts).

• Multi-currency and FX settlement experience.

• You've been through a safeguarding audit or a CASS 15 implementation.

• Experience with reconciliation or safeguarding tools, or scripting (Python) to automate recs.

• Exposure to setting up operations for a new entity or EU licence.

data.title: Founders' Office - Growth
data.description:
Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms, allowing you to run everything from your phone - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

We're already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $750m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

Why we're hiring

  • We're past product-market fit and growing 2x year on year, almost entirely through word of mouth, Google and AI search. Around 70 new leads land each month without a growth engine behind them, and you'll play a pivotal role in building one alongside the founders.

  • Our co-founder Paddy is taking direct ownership of growth, and he wants a commercially minded builder alongside him: someone who'd rather make the thing than talk about it.

  • You'll sit in the founders' office, working directly with Paddy on whatever moves the number most, from partnerships and events to building something that brings in 50 qualified leads in a month.

  • The goal is 7,000 deals a year. Getting there depends on more of the right people finding us.

What you'll build

You'll work directly with Paddy, our co-founder, with the freedom to try things fast and the backing to scale what works

  • Growth mechanisms: Lead magnets, micro products, tools and campaigns that bring syndicate leads and fund managers to Odin. You build the actual thing with AI, not a strategy deck about it. Think a calculator every new fund manager bookmarks, or a tool that turns a syndicate lead's first deal into a week's work instead of a month's. Ship it, see what works, double down.

  • Partnerships: Co-investors, syndicate networks, accelerators and fund admins already talk to the people we want to reach. You find the ones who can send us the right people and get them live.

  • Events: Pitch nights, GP-LP mixers and founder dinners for a community that backs everything from AI labs to small nuclear reactors. You'll turn that into new customers.

  • Referrals and repeat: Our existing customers already come back again and again. You'll build the ways they bring others with them.

  • Special projects: The founders' office gets the problems that matter and don't have an owner yet. You'll pick them up, work out what's true and get them done.

What we're looking for

  • Exceptionally sharp: At least a couple of years in a role that's trained you to think fast and rigorously. That might be consulting, banking, VC, a founder associate or chief of staff role, or early-stage growth.

  • A commercially minded builder: You love making things, and you think about who they're for and whether they'll move the number before you start.

  • You build with AI: You ship things yourself rather than waiting for someone else to execute your ideas, and you can show us what you've made.

  • Analytical and financially literate: You're comfortable with numbers, you can tell what's working from the data, and you understand how capital moves.

  • Taste and creative flair: You know what will land with a sophisticated audience of investors and founders, and what won't.

  • Fast-moving and self-directed: You make decisions without constant validation and you'd rather ship something today than perfect it next month.

  • Outcomes over activity: Pipeline and revenue are what you optimise for, not impressions or output volume.

  • Credible with investors: Comfortable on a call with a seasoned GP or in a room full of them.

  • Big plus: private markets exposure: VC, angel syndicates or fund admin. Useful, but not required.

How we work

There are five things we care about deeply:

  1. Reason from the ground up: Seek to understand what is true by always asking why. Do not trust convention or experts.

  2. Speed begets speed: We work fast. Speed compounds, it's the best form of defensibility, and it's energising to be around. If you work slowly, or tolerate slow work around you, you do not belong at Odin.

  3. Take ownership: Do not wait for permission to do things. Find the answer, force the thing into existence and hold others to an extremely high standard - the same standard you hold yourself to.

  4. Brutal honesty: If work doesn't meet the bar, people need to hear it, and the right people want to.

  5. Truly excellent customer service: Be a stickler for detail in every single interaction a customer has with us, and always strive to make this experience better, smoother, faster.

This role is probably not for you if

  • You want a well-defined lane and a fully built playbook;

  • You'd rather write the strategy than build and ship the thing yourself;

  • You need a team underneath you to get things done;

Salary

£60,000–£70,000 base, plus bonus and a meaningful equity grant.

Hiring process

Four stages: an intro call with Imani, our Head of People, a call with Paddy, a 90-minute build task, and a final with our founders. Detailed feedback within 24 hours of each one.

Location & ways of working

We're a London-based team. This role works side by side with the founders, and the speed we run at makes that much easier in person. At least three days a week in the office.

Benefits

  • Health: Private health insurance (Vitality), paid sick leave including support for pregnancy loss and fertility treatments

  • Parental Leave: Enhanced maternity, adoption, paternity and partner leave

  • Pension: 4% employer contribution with salary sacrifice options

  • Time Off: 25 days annual leave, 2 wellness days and flexible bank holidays (33 days total)

  • Work From Anywhere: Up to 6 weeks per year working from anywhere globally

  • Birthday Leave: An additional day of leave

data.title: Software Engineer, Product
data.description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the role

You'll work across LabOS — our internal software platform — building the orchestration layer that coordinates everything from experiment scheduling to execution to data capture and results processing. This is full-stack product engineering at the intersection of software and physical-world biology.

Day-to-day, that can mean things like:

  • Creating interfaces and APIs that give scientists and AI agents visibility into what's happening in the lab in real time

  • Building custom AI agents and tooling that automate decisions across the experiment lifecycle, from protocol design to troubleshooting failed results

  • Turning proprietary hardware into API-controllable devices that agents and software can operate programmatically

  • Designing scheduling systems that coordinate dozens of lab instruments with complex dependency chains

You'll own large areas of the product. We're a small team where individual engineers have large impact on what gets built and how.

What we're looking for

  • Full-stack production experience. We use TypeScript, React, Node, Postgres, but what matters is you can work across the stack.

  • Product instinct. You've shipped, watched users, iterated, and shipped again.

  • Comfortable in ambiguity. You start from a goal, not a spec. You scope problems down, decide what to build and what to skip, and write your own plan when none exists.

  • Builds with AI. You use AI tools heavily, but you have enough experience without them to know what good looks like.

  • Curious about biology. No background required, but running real experiments in the physical world should excite you.

Application deadline

We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis.

Immersive’s growth has been fuelled by our values that underpin everything we do, here's how they relate to this role:

We exceed our customers and partners expectations by crafting products, services and experience that surprise, delight and ensuring they feel valued and supported every day.

data.title: Regional Director - Enterprise
data.description:
Why Conduct

The world's largest companies should move at the speed of their ideas. Too often, they move at the speed of the systems they run on.

Behind every process change or new product line sits an SAP landscape shaped by decades of custom code and complexity. Changes take months. Migrations can cost more than $100 million and take years.

Conduct is building the AI operating system that makes this complexity understandable and actionable, so enterprises can move faster and pursue bigger ambitions. Major enterprises already trust us with their most critical systems. We have secured partnerships with systems integrators and raised a $60 million Series A. Demand is outpacing our capacity to deliver.

The Role

Your opportunity is to win new ground for Conduct, land its most important customers, and build the team that makes it happen, inside a company in hyper-growth.

As Regional Director, Enterprise, you will recruit, develop and lead a high-performing sales team focused on winning Conduct's most strategic new enterprise accounts and bringing a new kind of technology to market. You will own recruitment, enablement and sales execution across your territory, building pipeline and coaching Enterprise Account Executives through complex buying processes.

The challenge is to build a team that earns the trust of major enterprises on decisions that matter to their business, and turns that trust into consistent wins. You will set the standard for how that team hires, develops and sells.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Build the team: recruit, ramp and retain exceptional Enterprise Account Executives, raising the bar with every hire

  • Coach your AEs to exceed monthly, quarterly and annual bookings objectives through accountability and disciplined execution

  • Win new ground: lead the push into new enterprise accounts and guide the team through complex buying processes on the systems customers' businesses run on

  • Bring innovation to market: help the team explain how Conduct makes complex enterprise systems understandable and actionable, and coach credible, value-led conversations with senior business and technical stakeholders

  • Enable proactive prospecting and rigorous qualification to build a healthy, predictable pipeline

  • Win landmark customers: build executive relationships and coach the team through complex negotiations inside large organisations

  • Set the operating rhythm of a region growing at pace: forecasting, pipeline inspection, territory planning and performance management

  • Plan territory coverage and resource allocation as new opportunities open up

  • Work across the company to turn customer insight into better outcomes and regional demand

  • Lead by example, setting the standard for how Conduct sells

What You'll Bring to the Role

Must-Have Qualifications

  • At least two years of experience recruiting and managing a successful direct software sales team, driving it toward its goals

  • Five or more years of quota-carrying field sales experience in a fast-paced, competitive market

  • Demonstrated ability to run a complex enterprise sales process from first conversation to close

  • A proven track record of consistently exceeding sales targets

  • Proven experience winning new business in the Enterprise segment

  • Ability to explain the business value of complex enterprise technology to senior business and technical stakeholders

  • Skill in building business champions, including at executive level

  • Strong experience coaching and developing sales professionals, and helping them grow their careers

  • Comfort selling change on critical systems, and thriving in a fast-growing company where the market is still being won

  • Driven, competitive and motivated by meaningful results

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience selling into large enterprises running SAP or other complex enterprise systems

  • Familiarity with enterprise software, AI, or transformation and migration programmes

  • Training in sales qualification techniques such as MEDDIC

  • Experience leading customer expansion, cross-sell and land-and-expand strategies

  • Experience working alongside systems integrators and technology partners

data.title: Strategic Account Manager - Enterprise Hospitality (Paris)
data.description:
Lightspeed is looking for an experienced, strategically minded Strategic Account Manager to develop, engage, and closely support our most important enterprise customers in the hospitality segment over the long term.

In this role, you will act as the primary point of contact for our largest hospitality customers in France. You will be responsible for driving growth, product adoption, and stakeholder management within your portfolio, with the goal of building true business partnerships. You will leverage data, customer feedback, and your SaaS expertise to create value at the enterprise level.

***Please note that this role is based in Paris and follows a hybrid working model***



What you’ll do

  • Act as the main point of contact for our largest and most strategic hospitality customers

  • Develop and execute strategic account plans to drive growth, retention, and product adoption

  • Proactively work on increasing product usage and ensure Net Revenue Retention (NRR) grows across your portfolio

  • Plan and lead quarterly business reviews and success plans

  • Analyze usage data, go-live milestones, and health scores to identify and mitigate risks early

  • Build strong, trusted relationships with C-level and operational stakeholders, positioning Lightspeed as a long-term strategic partner

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Customer Success, Implementation, and Support teams to deliver an excellent customer experience

  • Collect customer feedback and proactively share it with relevant teams to identify product gaps and optimize the overall customer journey


What you bring

  • 3–5+ years of experience in Account Management or Strategic Customer Success within a B2B SaaS environment, ideally with enterprise customers

  • A strong understanding of SaaS metrics (NRR, product adoption, expansion, renewals, churn) and the ability to use them to manage your portfolio

  • A strong sense of ownership; you are hands-on, data-driven, and highly skilled in relationship management

  • Experience managing complex, multi-level stakeholder structures and confidently engaging with C-level, operations, and technical teams

  • Fluent business-level French and English

  • Experience in the hospitality, POS, or hospitality tech industry is a plus, but not required


What’s in it for you?

Come live the Lightspeed experience…

  • Genuine career opportunities in a company that’s creating new jobs every day

  • Work in a team large enough for growth but lean enough to make a real impact

  • Exposure to modern and proven technology

  • Ability to work and grow in a truly flexible environment

  • Opportunity to learn, expand your skill set, forge wonderful relationships and make your mark within the diverse and inclusive Lightspeed culture, a true Canadian tech success story

    … and enjoy a range of benefits that’ll keep you happy, healthy and (not) hungry:

  • Lightspeed equity scheme (we are all owners)

  • Health & Wellness Credit- expense up to 400 EUR per year towards your gym membership, yoga classes, a new bike or whatever else you do for your health

  • Mental Health Support through the Modern Health App- whether it is meditation, coaching or counseling you need - each employee gets access to this platform

  • People Experience - Our PX benefit allows you to work from pretty much anywhere in the world for 60 days a year 

  • Time off to volunteer and give back to your community

  • Transit benefit if you travel by public transport to the office

  • Lunch reimbursement on the days you work from our Paris office

  • Health insurance with attractive guarantee plans

 

We know that people are more than what’s on their CV. If you’re unsure that you have the right profile for the role... hit the ‘Apply’ button and give it a try!

To all recruitment agencies: Lightspeed does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. If we have not directly engaged your company in writing to supply candidates for a specific vacancy, Lightspeed will not be responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

Lightspeed is a proud equal opportunity employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive and barrier-free workplace. Lightspeed welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

Where to from here?

Obviously, this has to be mutually beneficial: we want you to step into a role you love, and we want to offer you a place you’re proud to come to every day. For a glimpse into our world check out our career page here.

Lightspeed is building communities through commerce, and we need people from all backgrounds and lived experiences to do that. We were founded in 2005, in Montreal’s gay village and our original members were all part of the LGBTQ+ community. The ethos of our business has been about inclusion from the very beginning, and we strive to provide a workplace where everyone belongs.

Who we are:

Powering the businesses that are the backbone of the global economy, Lightspeed's one-stop commerce platform helps merchants innovate to simplify, scale, and provide exceptional customer experiences. Our cloud commerce solution transforms and unifies online and physical operations, multichannel sales, expansion to new locations, global payments, financial solutions, and connection to supplier networks.

Founded in Montréal, Canada in 2005, Lightspeed is dual-listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: LSPD) and Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: LSPD). With teams across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, the company serves retail, hospitality, and golf businesses in over 100 countries.

Lightspeed handles your information in accordance with our Applicant Privacy Statement.

data.title: Associate Team Lead - Customer Support (T2)
data.description:
Résumé

Nous recherchons un(e) Associate Team Lead Support N2 / Chef(fe) d’équipe Support N2 pour rejoindre l’équipe Support Niveau 2 de Pennylane, au service des dirigeants d’entreprise et des cabinets comptables.

Pennylane est une plateforme de gestion financière et comptable qui accompagne les dirigeants d’entreprise et les cabinets d’expertise comptable dans leur quotidien. L’équipe Support Niveau 2 intervient sur les demandes les plus complexes ou nécessitant une expertise métier et produit approfondie, en lien avec les équipes Support Niveau 1, Support Technique, Produit et Tech.

Ce rôle est un poste de management de proximité : tu seras le relais opérationnel du Team Lead Support N2 et accompagneras une équipe de 6 à 12 agents au quotidien pour leur permettre de répondre aux utilisateurs avec efficacité, qualité et empathie. Tu contribueras également au pilotage de l’activité, à l’amélioration continue du support et à des projets transverses.

Notre culture

Au sein du Support, nous valorisons la transparence, la bonne ambiance, l’entraide et la résilience.

Nous restons proches de la réalité de nos utilisateurs, notamment des dirigeants d’entreprise et des professionnels de la comptabilité, afin de traiter chaque demande avec expertise métier, maîtrise du produit et empathie. Cette approche s’inscrit dans la culture Pennylane de Supporting SMEs et de proximité avec les utilisateurs.

Nous encourageons le feedback dans les deux sens, le développement de chacun et la prise d’initiative. Nous accordons de l’importance à l’autonomie, à la responsabilité et à la confiance, dans l’esprit de Community of Builders et de Radical Trust.

Concrètement, ton quotidien ressemblera à ça

  • Animer les points d’équipe et suivre la charge quotidienne.

  • Accompagner les agents sur leurs tickets, leurs priorités et leurs situations complexes.

  • Réaliser des écoutes ou analyses de conversations pour donner du feedback constructif.

  • Suivre les indicateurs de performance et de qualité de l’équipe, comme le temps de première réponse, le temps de résolution, la satisfaction client et le volume de tickets traités.

  • Participer aux rituels de pilotage opérationnel : suivi de la charge, priorisation des demandes, identification des alertes et coordination avec les autres équipes Support.

  • Remonter les irritants utilisateurs aux équipes Produit, Tech ou Ops.

  • Contribuer à améliorer les process, la documentation et les outils internes.

Responsabilités

  • Manager une équipe de 6 à 12 agents sous la supervision du Team Lead Support N2, en les accompagnant dans leur activité quotidienne, leur progression et leur épanouissement professionnel.

  • Donner des feedbacks clairs, réguliers et transparents, réaliser des écoutes et analyses de conversations, suivre les bilans et plans d’accompagnement individuels, proposer des coachings et identifier les besoins de formation.

  • Suivre les indicateurs de l’équipe et contribuer à la qualité du support, notamment le temps de première réponse, la satisfaction client, le temps de résolution, le volume traité, la prise en charge des nouveaux tickets et le suivi des tickets en cours.

  • Participer aux rituels de pilotage et à la gestion des files de demandes communes, notamment lors des rotations de permanence, en identifiant les alertes et en remontant les besoins de renfort ou d’arbitrage.

  • Être force de proposition pour optimiser les process, les outils, la documentation et les modes de fonctionnement du Support.

  • Collaborer avec les équipes support de niveau 1, l’équipe technique, les équipes opérationnelles ainsi que les équipes produit et tech, faire remonter les irritants utilisateurs et contribuer aux projets transverses.

  • Partager les bonnes pratiques avec les autres Associate Team Leads et contribuer à maintenir une communication fluide au sein du Support.

  • Prendre ponctuellement en charge des demandes internes urgentes ou des situations complexes nécessitant l’expertise du Support Niveau 2, en sachant orienter ou escalader lorsque cela est nécessaire.

Ce poste est fait pour toi si

  • Tu aimes accompagner une équipe et faire progresser les autres.

  • Tu sais garder du recul dans des situations opérationnelles parfois urgentes.

  • Tu es à l’aise avec les indicateurs, tout en gardant toujours en tête la qualité de l’expérience utilisateur.

  • Tu sais communiquer avec clarté, même quand les sujets sont complexes.

  • Tu as envie de contribuer à structurer une équipe Support dans un environnement en forte évolution.

Qualifications

  • Diplôme Bac+2 ou Bac+3 minimum en comptabilité, management ou dans un domaine équivalent.

  • Expérience d’au moins 1 an en management ou en accompagnement d’équipe, idéalement dans le secteur du support.

  • Bonne capacité à analyser une situation, prendre une décision mesurée et proposer des solutions concrètes.

  • Excellentes capacités de communication et de collaboration, avec assertivité et diplomatie.

  • Goût pour le feedback, la pédagogie et l’accompagnement individuel.

  • Aisance avec les outils informatiques, notamment les outils de ticketing et de documentation comme Intercom, Zendesk ou Notion.

  • Capacité à s’adapter à un environnement en évolution rapide.

  • Sens du service et attention portée à l’expérience utilisateur.

Les nice to have

Ces éléments sont un plus, mais ne sont pas indispensables si tu as une forte appétence pour le support, le management de proximité et l’apprentissage produit/métier.

  • Connaissances en comptabilité.

  • Expérience préalable en tant que contributeur individuel au sein d’une équipe Support.

  • Expérience dans un environnement SaaS ou start-up.

  • Expérience dans le management d’une équipe principalement à distance.

  • Expérience de collaboration avec des équipes Produit, Tech ou Ops.

  • Anglais niveau B1 minimum.

  • Utilisation de l’IA pour optimiser ses tâches.

Modalités pratiques

  • Tu reporteras au Team Lead Support N2.

  • Le rôle combine management de proximité, pilotage opérationnel et contribution ponctuelle sur des situations complexes ou urgentes.

  • L’équipe collabore principalement en français, avec des interactions possibles en anglais selon les sujets et les équipes.

🇫🇷 Données personnelles

Pennylane traite vos données pour gérer votre candidature et évaluer votre adéquation au poste. Si votre candidature n’aboutit pas, vos données peuvent être conservées 2 ans à compter de notre dernier échange ou de la clôture du recrutement afin de constituer & gérer un vivier de candidats. Vous pouvez vous opposer à tout moment et demander la suppression de vos données en écrivant à :
Notre data policy

🇬🇧 Personal Data

Pennylane processes your data to manage your application and assess your suitability for the position. If your application is unsuccessful, your data may be retained for 2 years from our last exchange or the closing of the recruitment process, in order to build and manage a candidate pool. You may object at any time and request the deletion of your data by writing to Learn more

🇩🇪 Personenbezogene Daten

Pennylane verarbeitet Ihre Daten, um Ihre Bewerbung zu bearbeiten und Ihre Eignung für die Stelle zu beurteilen. Sollte Ihre Bewerbung nicht erfolgreich sein, können Ihre Daten bis zu 2 Jahre ab unserem letzten Austausch oder dem Abschluss des Rekrutierungsverfahrens gespeichert werden, um einen Kandidatenpool aufzubauen und zu verwalten. Sie können jederzeit Widerspruch einlegen und die Löschung Ihrer Daten beantragen, indem Sie an Mehr erfahren

🇪🇸 Datos personales

Pennylane trata sus datos para gestionar su candidatura y evaluar su idoneidad para el puesto. En caso de que su candidatura no sea seleccionada, sus datos podrán conservarse hasta 2 años a partir de nuestro último contacto o de la finalización del proceso de selección, con el fin de constituir y gestionar una reserva de candidatos. Puede oponerse en cualquier momento y solicitar la eliminación de sus datos escribiendo a Más información
